title: Compatible finite local stage lifts from affine lifting
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preorder, $D:I^{op}\to Scheme$ a system of qcqs schemes with affine transition maps, $c$ a limit cone [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], $i_0$ a stage, $G$ a sheaf of sets on $D(i_0)$, and $W_0$ a qcqs etale object over $D(i_0)$. Assume the affine lifting property [lem-weil-pbc-sets-section-lift-affine] for every affine qcqs etale object over $D(i_0)$. For every limit section $t$ on the base change of $W_0$, there are a natural number $n$, affine etale objects $V_b$ over $D(i_0)$ and arrows $f_b:V_b\to W_0$ indexed by $Fin(n)$, a stage $j$ in $Over(i_0^{op})$, and sections $s_b$ on the stage base changes of $V_b$, with these properties: the base changes of the family $f_b$ are covering in the small etale topology at stage $j$ and at the limit; for every pair of stage arrows $a:Y\to V_{b,j}$ and $a^{\prime}:Y\to V_{b^{\prime},j}$ with equal composites into $W_{0,j}$, the restrictions of $s_b$ and $s_{b^{\prime}}$ along these arrows are equal; and the canonical limit section comparison [def-weil-pbc-sets-section-comparison] sends each $s_b$ to the restriction of $t$ along the limit base change of $f_b$. This assertion constructs local compatible representatives, not a section on the whole stage object.

source.document: Stacks Project, Étale Cohomology and Sites (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu)

proof.text: Construct the finite affine open cover directly with W₀.left.affineCover.finiteSubcover and reindex by Fin n. Its arrows cover by the range criterion. The affine sources have qcqs structure maps to the qcqs base. Base-change preservation gives the stage and limit covering clauses. Apply haff to each restriction of t, choose representatives, and use IsCofiltered.inf_objs_exists on their finite set of stages. Transport them with transition comparisons. The cone coherence law proves the required image equation at the common stage.

Naturality of the comparison is obtained directly from the composite natural transformation defining it. For any base arrows with equal composites into W₀, their restrictions of t agree by functoriality. Naturality and the image equations therefore give the hypothesis of finite matching. Apply the finite-matching theorem to the given family and lifts. Retain the affine objects and cover arrows, and transport their sections to its later stage. Cone coherence retains their images and base-change preservation retains both coverings. This constructs only the compatible family, without gluing. The cofiltered finite-set choice covers n=0 as well.
